pl-l4d44c8-d1e115.summary: Asks whether aborted fetuses and monsters will rise, and in what form.

pl-l4d44c8-d1e118.summary: Quotes Augustine: the question of aborted fetuses arises, born in the womb but not able to be reborn; if we say those already formed will rise, it can somehow be tolerated; but who would not more readily think the unformed perish like seeds not conceived?
claims: Formed fetuses may rise; unformed ones likely do not.

pl-l4d44c8-d1e127.summary: Continues: when man begins to live in the womb, and whether there is a hidden life not yet shown by movement, may be scrupulously disputed; to deny that fetuses cut out to save mothers had lived seems shameless; from when a man begins to live he can die, and dying, wherever death came to him, I cannot see how he would not belong to the resurrection.
claims: Whoever began to live belongs to the resurrection.

pl-l4d44c8-d1e134.summary: Continues: monsters born and living, however briefly, are not to be denied resurrection, but nature will be corrected; the two-membered child reported from the East, which Jerome recorded, will rise not as one double man but as two, as if born twins; other monsters of great deformity will be restored to human form.
claims: Conjoined twins rise as two persons.

pl-l4d44c8.summary: Asks whether aborted fetuses and monsters will rise. Augustine: formed fetuses may be said to rise; unformed ones more likely perish like unconceived seeds; when life begins in the womb is a difficult question, but one who began to live can die and so rise. Monsters that are born and live, however briefly, will rise with nature corrected: the two-membered child reported by Jerome will rise as two men, and other deformities will be restored to human form.
claims: Formed fetuses will rise; unformed ones likely do not.
Whoever began to live can die and rise.
Monstrous births will rise with nature corrected.
